sections.h2: Where does a Knox County seller record a deed?
sections.html:
Knox County deeds are recorded by the county recorder in Mount Vernon, the county seat, after the county auditor has handled the transfer paperwork. The auditor's office is at 117 East High Street, Suite 120, Mount Vernon, OH 43050, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, with the real estate desk at 740-393-6745. Ask the Knox County Recorder's office for its counter hours, payment types and mailing rules before you send a deed anywhere.

Ohio keeps one recorder for each county. A seller near Fredericktown or in Gambier uses the same Mount Vernon office as a seller who lives in the city, so a deed signed anywhere in Knox County follows the same two stops: auditor first, recorder second.

sections.h2: What does the Knox County auditor charge when a deed transfers?
sections.html:
The auditor's home page states that the conveyance fee in Knox County is $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. Section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents for each transfer or entry of a lot or parcel. The recorder's own charges follow section 317.32, which splits each charge into a base fee and a housing trust fund fee of equal size.

Knox County deed charges drawn from the auditor's home page and Ohio Revised Code sections 317.32, 317.114 and 319.54
ChargeAmount as printed
Conveyance fee, paid to the auditor$3.00 per thousand dollars of sale price

Ask the recorder whether the surcharge is collected and what the total comes to for your page count.

sections.h2: Who signs the statement of value, and who pays the fee?
sections.html:
Under section 319.202, the buyer or the buyer's representative files the statement of value, while the seller pays the conveyance fee. A county that has adopted a transfer tax collects that too, from the seller, before the deed goes to the recorder. The statute defines value as the full consideration for the property, and that figure includes any mortgage or vendor's lien on it.

The Knox County Auditor's forms page lists the paper a typical sale needs:

  • DTE 100, the conveyance fee statement of value and receipt.
  • DTE 100(EX), the statement of reason for exemption, used when no fee is due.
  • DTE 101, the statement of conveyance of homestead property, for a parcel that carries a homestead reduction.
  • DTE 102, the statement of conveyance of current agricultural use valuation property, which matters on Knox County farm acreage.

The statute bars anyone from willfully falsifying the stated value, so enter the real price.

sections.h2: Which Knox County transfers carry no conveyance fee?
sections.html:
Section 319.54(G)(3) lists the deeds that skip the auditor's fee. The seller or heir writes the matching reason on the exemption statement. The ones that come up most for house sellers and families:

  • A gift between spouses, or between a parent and a child or that child's spouse.
  • A transfer among the heirs or devisees of one decedent when nobody pays money for the property.
  • A deed into or out of a revocable trust, where the grantor kept an unlimited power to revoke.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one that was already signed and recorded.
  • A transfer ordered by a court, to the extent it is not a sale carried out under the order.
  • A transfer where the value of the interest is $100 or less.

The section carries more exceptions than these, including government and charity transfers. When your deed is exempt, the auditor still expects the exemption form, so ask the real estate desk which one applies.

sections.h2: What format must a deed follow before the Knox County recorder takes it?
sections.html:
Section 317.114 sets the layout rules. The recorder must accept a deed that breaks them but charges the extra $10 plus $10 shown in the table. The rules call for:

  • Print no smaller than a size ten font.
  • Paper from 8.5 by 11 inches up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Black or blue ink with no highlighting.
  • One inch of blank margin on both sides and along the bottom of every page.
  • A three inch blank band across the top of page one, with the right half kept for the recorder's endorsement, and a one and one half inch band on later pages.

The rules skip court and taxing authority documents, plats, state or federal agency papers and anything signed before July 1, 2009. Page numbers, initials and bar codes in the margins draw no extra fee.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Knox County itself?
sections.html:
Knox County was formed from Fairfield County in 1808 and takes its name from Henry Knox. It covers 525.50 square miles of land, and Wikipedia reports that about 58 percent of it is farmland and 28 percent forest. Most of the county sits in the glaciated Allegheny Plateau, with rolling hills and valleys. Mount Vernon is the only city.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows 64,002 residents in July 2025, up 2.0 percent from the April 2020 base, and 26,668 housing units. Owners occupy 75.5 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $239,400 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $950. Median household income is $73,878, and workers average 25.7 minutes getting to their jobs.

Employers named on the county's Wikipedia page include Siemens Energy and Ariel Corporation in Mount Vernon, Kenyon College in Gambier, Mount Vernon Nazarene University and Kokosing Construction near Fredericktown.

sections.h2: When are Knox County real estate taxes due, and how do you contest a value?
sections.html:
The auditor's page printed 2026 due dates of February 13 for the first half and August 26 for the second half of real estate taxes, so both have passed. Ask the Knox County Treasurer or the auditor for the 2027 dates, and use the treasurer link on the auditor's home page to see what a parcel owes.

Complaints against a valuation go to the Knox County Board of Revision. The auditor's public notice says the board holds its organization meeting on January 4, 2027, and that formal complaints for that year must be filed between January 1, 2027 and March 31, 2027. The same notice says the 2026 returns are open for inspection at the auditor's office during its regular hours.

A seller with a tax bill still open at closing usually settles it through the title company. Request the payoff figure early, since the second half of a tax year can arrive after the contract is signed.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Knox County, Ohio?
faqs.a: The Knox County Recorder in Mount Vernon records it. The deed goes to the county auditor at 117 East High Street, Suite 120 first, so the auditor can take the statement of value and collect the conveyance fee. Ask the recorder's office for its current hours and mailing instructions.

faqs.q: How much is the Knox County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's home page states $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. Section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents for each transfer or entry. The seller pays the fee under section 319.202.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed does not follow the margin and ink rules?
faqs.a: The recorder still accepts it but charges an extra $10 base fee and $10 housing trust fund fee under section 317.114. Court documents, plats, state and federal agency papers and anything signed before July 1, 2009 are outside the rule.

faqs.q: Can I deed a Knox County house to my children without paying the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: A gift between a parent and a child, or that child's spouse, is on the exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3). You file the exemption statement (DTE 100 EX) with the auditor and the fee is waived. The deed still has to be recorded, and the recorder's own charges still apply.

faqs.q: What do I need if the Knox County parcel has a homestead reduction or farm valuation?
faqs.a: The auditor's forms page lists DTE 101 for homestead property and DTE 102 for current agricultural use valuation property. Section 319.202 also asks the buyer to confirm that the seller was asked about both. For farm ground, ask the auditor about any recoupment charge before closing.
